intro: The Debtors ran the auction on Nov 5, 2026 (virtual, via Zoom) and filed the Notice of Auction Results on Nov 6. Every bid below is still "subject to agreement on definitive documentation", and the final asset purchase agreements control over the notice's summary. As of the Nov 9 objection deadline the Debtors had not filed an asset purchase agreement, a list of designated contracts, or a proposed sale order (Docket #443, para. 8). The court has not yet approved any sale; the Sale Hearing is Nov 16, 2026 at 1:00 PM ET.

gov_rules.headline: No buyer gets a federal contract automatically.
points: Under 11 U.S.C. 365(c)(1) and the Anti-Assignment Act (41 U.S.C. 6305), the US says no federal contract may be assumed or assigned without its written consent, and it has not given consent (Docket #297 and #443).
Consent comes through the FAR novation process, decided by each contracting officer, and the US says it generally happens after the sale closes (Docket #297, para. 16).
The US asked that any sale order make no finding on adequate assurance for federal contracts, set no cure amounts for them, and preserve the government's setoff and recoupment rights (Docket #443).

The cure schedule (Docket #252-1) lists 147 entries labeled "Government Contract", 123 of which appear to name a federal agency, mostly without contract numbers. It is a list of possible assumptions, not of contracts actually being sold.

Company-wide, the Debtors held more than 100 multi-award IDIQ contracts and 12 single-award IDIQ contracts (Docket #15, as cited in #443). The filings do not say whether any GSA-labeled entry is a Multiple Award Schedule contract, a blanket purchase agreement or an order.

by_unit.cure_schedule: GSA-labeled entries (about 19 by our read of the PDF) sit under Noble Supply & Logistics (about 13), Federal Resources Supply Company (3) and Tactical & Survival Specialties (3), including GSA Federal Acquisition Service, GSA General Products Acquisition Center, and GSA regional offices; one entry carries a number (7QSBPA-D6). Also DLA Aviation, DLA Land & Maritime (the US counts ten identical entries), DHS, DEA, DTRA and State.
by_unit.note: DFS is the bulk of the multi-award IDIQ base and the largest segment ($674M of 2025 revenue). The SOE contract (about $630M in 2025) had about $400M of orders terminated Aug 27, and the court let DLA terminate about 21,000 delivery orders (Docket #434). The filings do not map each Debtor entity to a segment, so the entity breakdown above is by Debtor, not by segment.

by_unit.cure_schedule: The long-term single-award programs sit here. The FSG-53 contract terminated in June 2026 (Docket #15). The Army depot supply-store obligation is among what DLA asked to end (Docket #325). Olive Branch and Holly Springs warehouse leases are on the cure schedule.
by_unit.note: The 12 single-award IDIQ contracts are described as capital-intensive. The two largest have been terminated or not renewed.

by_unit.cure_schedule: Two entries naming the Canadian Department of National Defence appear on the cure schedule. The Debtors have hired German counsel to terminate staff and wind up the German entity (Docket #383).

open_items: No asset purchase agreement, designated-contract list, or proposed sale order had been filed as of the Nov 9 objections or on the Nov 10 docket.

Sale-related objections filed Nov 9 are limited reservations of rights, not opposition to the sale: the United States (Docket #443), Rae Systems/Honeywell (#441), Bering Straits Professional Services (#446) and Oracle (#447).
Sale Hearing Nov 16, 2026 at 1:00 PM ET. Combined disclosure statement and plan of liquidation due Nov 14. Next omnibus hearing Dec 17, 2026.
